newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain tells regions to put freeze on suspect beef.
newsitem.headline: Spain tells regions to put freeze on suspect beef.

text.p: Spain told its regions to put a freeze beef that might have been imported illegally from Britain through Belgium.

"The Public Health Department of the Health and Consumer Ministry, through its warning network, has informed all the regions of the need for a cautionary freeze on any meat from that country or protected by sanitary seals from it," Spain said on Wednesday.
The European Commission said it was considering legal action against Britain for illegal exports of unspecified quantities of British beef to the European Union and other countries.

The EU banned exports of British beef and beef products in March 1996 to protect consumer health after the British government said it was possible a human form of the fatal mad cow disease, CJD, could be caught from eating infected beef.

In a statement, the European Parliament's socialist group quoted EU sources saying that the fraud was operated by a firm in Belgium which exported British beef under a Belgian label to Russia, Egypt and Bosnia as well as to Spain and France.
